findings.passage: “Voters have voiced their concerns loud and clear, and yet, the governor repeatedly said that he will veto legislation to increase the validity of the Commonwealth’s election process. Unfortunately, he still seems to be ruling without consideration of the majority of state residents, much like how he handled the pandemic for a year,” Sen. Stefano said. “It’s disappointing, but we can’t let that stop us from being responsive to Pennsylvanians’ needs.”
findings.note: Quote in his office's press release on Senate passage of SB 735, a proposed constitutional amendment asking voters whether ID should be required each time a ballot is cast. He criticises the governor's stated veto of election-process legislation. The release says he supported the measure. The original page is gone (404), so the archived copy is cited.

findings.passage: The Senate today approved a plan to allow voters to decide if the Pennsylvania Constitution should be amended to require identification each time a voter casts a ballot, according to Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32), who supported the measure.
findings.note: Opening line of the same press release from his office. It is the office's description, not a direct quote of him, and says he supported SB 735.

findings.passage: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the way we handle voting in Pennsylvania, and our social media platforms amplify any issues that arise. Clear communication and minor fixes to the election code will alleviate most of the concerns.
findings.note: His written answer in the WESA candidate survey, to a question about discontent with the two major political parties. He mentions voting rules only briefly. No mention of ID or citizenship.

findings.passage: The Senate moved to protect the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding citizens by approving Senate Bill 822, which strengthens Pennsylvania’s state preemption over regulating firearms and ammunition, preventing local governments from enacting ordinances that are more restrictive than those established by the General Assembly.
findings.note: Office e-newsletter under his name, headed 'Protecting Pennsylvanians' Second Amendment Rights'; presents SB 822 (state preemption of local gun rules) as protecting gun rights.
subjects: local governments making stricter gun rules (state preemption)

findings.passage: Allowing local governments to establish a patchwork of inconsistent gun laws would make it impossible for Pennsylvania residents, along with citizens from other states, to travel without fear of inadvertently breaking a local law they were unaware of.
findings.note: Same newsletter; gives the reason for state preemption of local gun ordinances.
subjects: local governments making stricter gun rules (state preemption)

findings.passage: The Senate continued its work to reinforce Second Amendment protections with committee approval of legislation to allow law‑abiding adults who are legally permitted to own a firearm to carry concealed without the need for a government‑issued permit.
findings.note: Office e-newsletter, headed 'Committee Acts to Bolster Support of Constitutional Right to Bear Arms'; describes SB 357 (carry without a permit) approved in the Judiciary Committee.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: The Senate Judiciary Committee approved Senate Bill 357, which also preserves an optional License to Carry Firearms for reciprocity with other states and modernizes the permitting process by reducing investigation time from 45 to 14 days, updating terminology and removing outdated disqualifiers while keeping all prohibitions for individuals who may not legally possess a firearm.
findings.note: Same newsletter; describes what SB 357 keeps and changes (optional licence, shorter investigation time).
subjects: carry a gun without a permit
